missing_details: definition of the Reeb vector field
contact-type hypersurface condition in a symplectic manifold
refined_question: Let Σ be a regular compact hypersurface of contact type in a symplectic manifold (W,ω) — that is, there exists a Liouville vector field defined near Σ which is transverse to Σ, making Σ a contact-type level set Σ=H^{-1}(c) of some Hamiltonian H. Does the Hamiltonian flow on Σ admit at least one nonconstant periodic orbit?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, given a closed (compact without boundary) contact manifold (M,α) with contact form α and associated Reeb vector field R_α, does R_α admit at least one periodic orbit?
justification: The canonical formulation on Wikipedia states that on a compact contact manifold its Reeb vector field carries at least one periodic orbit; this directly translates to the Hamiltonian viewpoint via contact-type hypersurfaces in symplectic manifolds (any such level set yields a Reeb flow) (Definition; Equivalent)([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weinstein_conjecture)). The name “Weinstein conjecture” alone omits crucial hypotheses (compactness, contact form, Reeb vector field, periodic orbit, contact-type embedding, regularity of the level set), hence a low completeness score. Our refined question is faithful and self-contained, with no additional assumptions beyond the original conjecture.
